rv.q: Feeling Afraid is simultaneously a poignant exposure of one man’s stark emotional vulnerabilities and a very funny study of the often absurd realities of handling online dating in the modern world.
Steven Webb is brilliant as The Comedian.
The chatty, almost conspiratorial revelations are cynic-proof and disarmingly presented by an absolute pro and I loved it.
A genuine stand-up comedian would be hard-pressed to deliver a set as propulsively compelling, as hilarious, and as heartbreaking as Webb achieves.
An actor as a comedian works quite brilliantly, and Webb’s performance captures nuances and expressions that you wouldn’t necessarily get at an actual stand-up gig.
His ability to flip between two extremes so seamlessly is astonishing and a real joy to watch.
Marcelo Dos Santos’ lengthily titled play Feeling Afraid As If Something Terrible Is Going To Happen is a terrific tonic for today’s turmoil with Shucked ’s Steven Webb at the helm.
Ultimately, Feeling Afraid As If Something Terrible Is Going to Happen is an entertaining comedy elevated by an exceptional central performance, but a less compelling exploration of queer intimacy.

cn.t: Critics praise this darkly comic one-man show for Steven Webb's magnetic performance and Marcelo Dos Santos' sharp, perceptive writing. The blend of stand-up comedy and confessional theatre earns strong acclaim.
